questions.question:
D4 — Finding 2.1: the notification email has no error handling and an unspecified transaction boundary. How should the email leg fail?
Project/branch/task: main, Stripe payment webhook handler plan, HOLD SCOPE review.
ELI10: After we mark the user paid, we send them an email. Today's plan sends it inline with no error handling and does not say whether it runs inside the database transaction. If it is inside, a mail outage rolls back the payment and Stripe keeps retrying into the same outage for up to three days, so the user never gets marked paid. If it is outside and the error propagates, the ingress wrapper returns 500 and fires a "failed webhook" alert for a payment that actually committed, and the Stripe retry is then swallowed by dedup. Either way the plan leaves this to chance.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Users who paid stay unpaid during a mail outage, or on-call chases false webhook-failure alerts for committed payments.
Recommendation: A because zero silent failures plus explicit-over-clever: commit first, then rescue the mail client's named exceptions, log the correlated context, and return 200 so the existing mail failure alert and runbook carry the retry, exactly as the retained runbook contract describes.
Completeness: A=9/10, B=4/10
Net: A costs about 15 lines and one test each for delivery error and timeout; B costs nothing now and an incident later.

options.label: 2.1A Post-commit, rescue named mail errors, 200 (recommended)
options.description: Send the email only after the DB transaction commits and dedup records completion. Rescue the mail client's specific delivery and timeout exception classes (never StandardError), log at warn with event id, user id, payment intent id and the operation, then return 200. Verified by unit tests for provider 5xx and timeout asserting the user stays paid and the response is 200. Failure visibility: existing mail failure-rate dashboard and on-call alert. Human ~2h / CC ~10 min. ✅ A mail outage can never block or roll back a payment. ✅ No false "failed webhook" alerts; the mail alert plus runbook retry the notification only. ❌ A second, unrelated mail exception class would still propagate until named.

options.label: 2.1B Leave the email unhandled as planned
options.description: Keep the inline call with no rescue. Behavior depends on where the implementer puts the transaction boundary. Human 0 / CC 0. ✅ Zero additional code in the handler. ✅ If outside the transaction, the contract's 500-then-dedup path technically converges. ❌ If inside the transaction, a mail outage blocks payment recording for up to three days of Stripe retries; if outside, every mail failure raises a false webhook-failure alert.

D5 — Issue 1: the successful-charge test asserts only that the receipt is truthy, so it cannot detect a wrong receipt. Strengthen it to the stated contract?
Project/branch/task: plan-count-VaZa4U on main, /plan-ceo-review HOLD SCOPE, PLAN.md "Proposed tests" item 1 (lines 28-30).
ELI10: The plan's own contract section says a 1000-cent USD charge with Stripe id ch_paid must return exactly { chargeId: "ch_paid", amountCents: 1000, currency: "USD" }. The proposed test only checks that some object came back. A receipt with amountCents 100000, a missing chargeId, or currency "usd" would all pass. The test would be green while customers see wrong receipts.
Stakes if we pick wrong: A receipt-construction regression in payment code ships with a passing test that claims to cover it, which is worse than no test because it creates false confidence.
Recommendation: 1A because the plan's own contract states the exact values, the factory already returns the receipt, and an exact assertion costs one line (well-tested code is non-negotiable; explicit over clever).
Completeness: 1A=10/10, 1B=6/10, 1C=3/10
Pros / cons:
1A) Assert the exact receipt (recommended)
  ✅ Deep-equal the returned receipt to { chargeId: "ch_paid", amountCents: 1000, currency: "USD" }; any wrong field fails with a readable diff.
  ✅ Also rejects extra or missing fields, pinning the receipt shape the caller contract promises.
  ❌ If the receipt legitimately gains a field later, this test must be updated (that is the point).
1B) Assert the three fields individually
  ✅ Each field checked by name; a wrong amount fails naming the amount.
  ✅ Tolerates additional fields being added to the receipt without touching the test.
  ❌ Silently allows shape drift (extra or renamed fields) that the stated contract does not permit.
1C) Keep truthy-only as planned
  ✅ Zero change to the plan text; smallest possible test body.
  ✅ Cannot break when receipt fields change.
  ❌ Cannot distinguish a correct receipt from a wrong one; the stated contract is unverified.

D6 — Issue 2: the repeated-502 test asserts only the PaymentUnavailable rejection, so it cannot detect a broken retry loop. Also assert the attempt count and backoff record?
Project/branch/task: plan-count-VaZa4U on main, /plan-ceo-review HOLD SCOPE, PLAN.md "Proposed tests" item 2 (lines 31-34).
ELI10: The plan's contract section says: with max_retries=1, two 502s mean exactly two charge attempts, one recorded 100 ms backoff, then PaymentUnavailable. The proposed test checks only the final rejection. A regression that never retries (one attempt), retries five times, or skips the backoff entirely would still reject with PaymentUnavailable and pass. The factory already exposes the Stripe call history and the sleeper record, so the probes exist and are unused.
Stakes if we pick wrong: A retry-policy regression (hammering Stripe with no backoff, or giving up without retrying) ships with a green test that claims to cover retry exhaustion.
Recommendation: 2A because the contract states exact counts, the factory already exposes both probes, and the plan's rules forbid weakening an exact count to a lower bound (I err toward handling more edge cases; well-tested code is non-negotiable).
Completeness: 2A=10/10, 2B=6/10, 2C=3/10
Pros / cons:
2A) Assert rejection plus exact call history and sleeper record (recommended)
  ✅ Asserts rejection is a PaymentUnavailable instance, Stripe mock call history length is exactly 2, and the sleeper record equals [100].
  ✅ Catches no-retry, over-retry, and missing or wrong backoff, each with a specific failing assertion.
  ❌ Couples the test to the retry policy values (2 attempts, 100 ms), which is what pinning a contract means.
2B) Assert rejection plus call count only
  ✅ Catches no-retry and over-retry regressions via the mock call history.
  ✅ One extra assertion; does not touch the sleeper record.
  ❌ A retry loop that skips the backoff and hammers Stripe immediately still passes.
2C) Keep rejection-only as planned
  ✅ Zero change to the plan text; the error type is still verified.
  ✅ Immune to future retry-policy tuning.
  ❌ Cannot tell a working retry loop from a broken one; the stated attempt and backoff contract is unverified.
Net: a test that proves the retry policy versus a test that only proves the final error type.

Verification: locally set max_retries to 0 and to 2 and confirm the count assertion fails each way; drop the sleep call and confirm the sleeper assertion fails. (human: ~10 min / CC: ~2 min)

options.description: Assert rejects with PaymentUnavailable and call history length === 2. Backoff timing stays unverified. (human: ~5 min / CC: ~1 min)

D6 — Issue 2: the repeated-502 test asserts only that processPayment rejects with PaymentUnavailable. What should it assert?
Project/branch/task: `main`, PLAN.md proposed test 2 (two consecutive Stripe 502s, max_retries=1).
ELI10: PLAN.md states the contract: with max_retries=1 the operation makes exactly two charge attempts separated by one recorded 100 ms backoff, then rejects with PaymentUnavailable. The planned assertion checks only the rejection. A processPayment that never retries (one attempt), retries five times (over-charging risk against a flaky Stripe), or sleeps 0 ms or 10 s between attempts all still reject with PaymentUnavailable and pass. The factory already exposes the Stripe mock call history and the sleeper record, so the exact checks cost two lines.
Stakes if we pick wrong: a retry-loop regression (no retry, or unbounded retry) ships green; under a real Stripe outage that means either every customer fails on the first blip or the service hammers Stripe with duplicate attempts.
Recommendation: 2A because the contract names exact counts (two attempts, one 100 ms backoff) and the probes already exist; "never weaken an exact count to a lower bound" and "err on the side of handling more edge cases" both apply.
Completeness: A=10/10, B=7/10, C=3/10
Pros / cons:
2A) Assert rejection with PaymentUnavailable AND mock call history has exactly 2 entries AND sleeper record equals [100] (recommended) (human: ~15 min / CC: ~1 min)
  ✅ Catches no-retry, over-retry, wrong backoff duration, and extra backoffs; every failure names the attempt count or the recorded delays
  ✅ Uses only the probes the plan already says the factory exposes; no new test infrastructure
  ❌ Three assertions in one test; if all three regress at once the first failure masks the others until it is fixed
2B) Assert rejection AND exactly 2 attempts, skip the backoff record (human: ~10 min / CC: ~1 min)
  ✅ Catches no-retry and over-retry regressions, the two costliest failure modes
  ✅ One fewer line than 2A
  ❌ A backoff of 0 ms (hot retry loop against a failing Stripe) or 10 s (user waits) passes silently
2C) Keep rejection-only as planned
  ✅ Zero additional lines beyond the sketch
  ✅ Cannot break if the retry schedule is later tuned
  ❌ Cannot distinguish a working retry loop from no retry loop at all
Net: two lines against probes that already exist versus a test blind to the retry behavior it was written to protect.
